name: attention_excursion_b1
brief: prompts/attention_excursion.md -- Part II (Brief 1), as amended by prompts/attention_excursion_b1_amendment_1.md, ..._amendment_2.md and ..._amendment_3.md. prompts/attention_excursion_b1.md is kept as the as-run record.
type: build -- not a phase. Builds instruments and controls; reads no attention-versus-outcome relationship anywhere, including on the dev sample. Ends at a HARD STOP (T7).
received_truncated: Run 1 (dec1d70 -> stop a3f6a9c) ran from a paste truncated at 50,000 characters. The complete document is now filed; lines 1-739 are identical. Escalation rows 6-7, II.4, II.5 and Part III come from the complete text.

population.sidecar_rule: listed alongside the dev sample and carried as its own row everywhere; never pooled; not used in T6 controls (the 50 are the control population)
population.event_folder: data/filtered/{ticker}_{event_date_canonical}_{momentum_pct} -- momentum_pct resolves the folder path only (D4)
population.repair_siblings: trades_repair_1c.parquet is read alongside trades.parquet wherever present (CLAUDE.md repair-provenance rule); heal writes fill genuine absence only, so the union has no duplicate rows by construction

slices.rule: chronological by event_date_canonical (D38); dev and sidecar events -> dev_quarantine regardless of date
slices.first_seen_slice: earliest of development < selection < final in which the ticker has any D1 event (dev_quarantine rows are assigned by their date for this purpose, so a quarantined event still marks its ticker as seen)
slices.is_first_seen_ticker: TRUE when the event's own slice equals its ticker's first_seen_slice; FALSE for dev_quarantine rows

t2_tau.rule: first print on the event day at or after 04:00 ET, in (sip_timestamp, sequence_number) order, with price >= 1.30 x prior_close_exact, excluding a print that fails the spike guard
t2_tau.search_start: 04:00 ET on event_date_canonical (DST resolved by the tz database)

spike_guard.neighbours: immediate predecessor and successor in the full sorted print sequence of the folder
spike_guard.rule: spike iff |p_i - p_(i-1)|/p_(i-1) > 0.03 AND |p_i - p_(i+1)|/p_(i+1) > 0.03 AND |p_(i-1) - p_(i+1)|/max(p_(i-1), p_(i+1)) <= 0.03; a print with no successor is not a spike; a spike cannot set tau, the search continues
spike_guard.discrepancy_recorded: The brief calls this 'the exit overlay's construction' but states neighbour agreement at 3%. The overlay's code (research/participation_exit_overlay/common.py) used spike_threshold/2 = 1.5%. The brief's stated 3% is used; tau under the overlay's 1.5% is computed alongside as a diagnostic and the difference counted.

t2_tau.int64: tau_ns is int64 end to end; never float64
t2_tau.segment: research/phase_10c/common.py::assign_segment on the tau print's own condition codes, event-day open/close from the calendar
t2_tau.proxy: results/relative_momentum/v1/artifacts/t5_d1_candidate_moments.parquet (first trade of the minute whose high reached +30% over the minute-bar prior close)
t2_tau.decomposition_diagnostic: tau is also computed against the minute-bar prior close (tau_mb). tau_mb - tau_proxy isolates the print-vs-minute-stamp difference; tau_exact - tau_mb isolates the prior-close change. Diagnostic only.
t2_tau.facets: shares and prints from 04:00 to tau inclusive (the speed facet of Part I I.6a)

amendment_1.proxy_prime: tau_proxy_prime = the v1 minute-level proxy recomputed from ticks with the SAME prior close as tau_exact: the first clock minute (floor((ts - 04:00 ET)/60 s), from 04:00) whose maximum print price is >= 1.30 x the revised close, stamped at the first print of that minute. No spike guard -- the proxy's minute high never had one.
amendment_1.proxy_prime_validation: the same construction with the minute-bar close must reproduce v1's stored proxy (t5_d1_candidate_moments.parquet, float64, 256 ns grid) to within 1 microsecond on the events both define; the reproduction rate is reported

tau_close_sensitive.rule: TRUE when |tau(revised close) - tau(minute-bar close)| > 60 s; when exactly one of the two exists, TRUE (the close choice decides whether the event crosses at all) with tau_gap_close_s NULL; when neither exists, NULL
tau_close_sensitive.use: a facet on every later panel, never a filter (A1.3)

amendment_1.guard15: tau_ns_guard15 carried as a sensitivity column (A1.4); the count where it differs is reported

t3_open_boundary.clock_minute: derived from first_trade_ts, floor((first_trade_ts - 04:00 ET) / 60 s) -- not minute_index, whose post-segment indexing was found inconsistent earlier in this line
t3_open_boundary.normaliser: the event's own median n_trades over the event day's existing bars (minutes with >= 1 trade), 04:00-20:00
t3_open_boundary.empty_minute: a clock minute with no bar contributes normalised rate 0 (it is a measured zero, not missing)
t3_open_boundary.pre_0400_note: the table holds no bars before 04:00; 03:55-03:59 therefore carry n = 0 and are drawn as such
t3_open_boundary.post_tau_exclusion: a minute is included only if it ends at or before tau (minute_start + 60 s <= tau_ns); the tau minute itself is excluded
t3_open_boundary.events_without_tau: prior close available but never crossing -> every minute included (no crossing to exclude); prior close unavailable -> excluded (tau cannot be placed); both counted
t3_open_boundary.proposal_rule: for open O in {04:00, 09:30}: L(m) = median of the per-minute medians over clock minutes [m+10, m+20]; proposed boundary = first minute m >= O with p25(m) <= L(m) <= p75(m). Also reported: the first m from which the condition holds for 5 consecutive minutes. Cooper confirms or replaces at T7.

t4_excursion.path: every print with sip_timestamp strictly > tau_ns and <= 20:00 ET on the event day (DA-1). Prints sharing tau's timestamp belong to the attention side (<= tau), never to the path.
t4_excursion.bucketing: equal share volume; a print larger than a bucket's remaining capacity is split across buckets at its own price; bucket price = VWAP; bucket time = timestamp of the last print contributing to it
t4_excursion.positions: tau is position 0 (u = 0, price = tau_price); bucket i sits at u = i/N (its completed cumulative volume share)
t4_excursion.returns: r_1 = ln(P_1 / tau_price), r_i = ln(P_i / P_(i-1)) for i = 2..N -- N returns
t4_excursion.sigma_b: sqrt((pi/2) * mean_i |r_i| |r_(i-1)|) over the N-1 adjacent pairs (bipower variation, Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard 2004)
t4_excursion.peak: argmax over positions 0..N of the log price; first occurrence on ties

components.rise_s: (ln P_peak - ln tau_price) / sigma_path  (>= 0; 0 when the peak is tau itself)
components.dip_before_peak_s: largest drawdown of the log path over positions 0..i_peak / sigma_path
components.fall_bp: (P_peak - P_N) / tau_price * 1e4  -- both money heights are relative to the entry-instant price, the basis the cost stack is quoted on
components.t_peak_s: bucket time of the peak - tau (0 when the peak is tau)

edge_classes.rise_censored: peak in the last bucket (i_peak = N)
edge_classes.no_rise: peak at tau or in the first bucket (i_peak <= 1); peak_at_tau (i_peak = 0, rise_s = 0) carried separately -- the brief's T4 says 'first bucket', Part I I.2c says 'at tau'; both are carried
edge_classes.halt_in_path: any inter-print gap > 60 s inside the path, plus LULD-V3c halt labels overlapping the path where they exist (research/participation_exit_overlay/common.py::load_halt_labels)
edge_classes.thin_path: fewer than 250 prints after tau -- declared, not derived; still computed where possible

t5_attention.population: dev sample (50) + sidecar (6, own row); the cross-sectional axis reads every D1 event live on those dates
t5_attention.causality: every attention quantity uses prints with sip_timestamp <= tau_ns only; an assertion raises if any print with sip_timestamp > tau reaches one (escalation row 3)
t5_attention.collapse: research/scale_field/subsecond_origin.py::collapse_tol at 10 ms (D26 identity collapse); raw print counts carried alongside; share and dollar volume use all prints (unaffected by collapsing)

a1_turnover.numerator: shares traded from 04:00 ET to tau inclusive (all prints)
a1_turnover.assertion: shs_asof_ns < tau_ns per event; a violation is a LOG row (escalation row 5) and the event's turnover is 'unavailable', not computed
a1_turnover.also_logged: shs_accepted_ns >= tau_ns is logged as a second, stricter check (the count is knowable at acceptance, not at the as-of date); it does not change availability, which follows the brief's asof rule
a1_turnover.states: unavailable (no count / asof violation / zero artifact), zero (no shares traded before tau), and a value are three distinct states

a2_acceleration.accel_k: ln(n_recent / n_older); n_recent = collapsed trades in [tau - W_k/2, tau], n_older = collapsed trades in [tau - W_k, tau - W_k/2)

counting_noise_stop.derivation: SE of a log count ratio ~ sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2); resolving ln 2 = 0.693 at two SE needs sqrt(2/n) <= 0.347, so n >= 16.7 -> 17. Carried, not tuned.

a2_acceleration.floor_note_before_run: With both halves >= 17 the floor needs n_recent + n_older >= 4.51, which the counting stop already guarantees; the D22 floor is therefore expected never to be the binding stop. Recorded before the run so it can be checked, not discovered.
a2_acceleration.descend_rule: descend while both stops pass; the first rung where either fails is recorded with its reason and is not valid
a2_acceleration.from_nothing: n_older = 0 with n_recent > 0 -> class from_nothing on that rung; never a numeric +inf

kernel_check.estimator: research/scale_field/scale_field.py::field_exact with kernel='onesided' (D23), evaluated at t = tau on the collapsed prints in [04:00, tau]
kernel_check.edge_rule: undefined where the history tau - 04:00 is shorter than truncate x scale, truncate = 4 -- the scale field's own causal edge rule (field_onesided). With scales W_k and W_k/2 this defines the kernel version on rungs k >= 2 only.
kernel_check.comparison: per-rung Spearman between count and kernel versions across events; disagreement reported, not resolved

a3_catalyst.why_not_event_fundamentals_alone: event_fundamentals' flg_ columns are relative to Build F1's t0, not tau. Where tau precedes t0 a filing counted there can post-date tau (a lookahead); where tau follows t0 a filing in (t0, tau) is missed. The tau-relative quantities are therefore rebuilt from the same raw source F1 used.
a3_catalyst.source: data/raw/fundamentals/sec/2026-09-12/submissions/{cik}.json (+ older-history files), F1's own raw archive; fields and accepted_ns parsing as research/fundamentals_f1/t3_filing_index.py; CIK from event_fundamentals (D30: CIK as of t0, never ticker)
a3_catalyst.filing_24h: any filing with tau - 24 h <= accepted_ns < tau
a3_catalyst.assertion: no filing with accepted_ns >= tau_ns enters any A3 quantity

cross_sectional.live_set: every D1 event on the same event_date_canonical with tau_i <= tau_j <= tau_i + L (j included); rest_of_session = tau_i <= tau_j
cross_sectional.flow_share_k: j's dollar volume / the live set's total dollar volume over (tau_j - W_k, tau_j], for each of j's valid A2 rungs; identical clock windows for every name
cross_sectional.accel_rank_k: rank of j on accel_k among live names, every name counted over j's windows; only names clearing the counting-noise stop on that window are ranked; rank 1 = highest; n ranked carried
cross_sectional.per_live_name: move_at at tau_j = last print <= tau_j / its own prior_close_exact - 1; seconds since its own tau
cross_sectional.causality: every live name's prints are cut at tau_j, asserted

t5b_competition.scope: dates of the 50 dev events only (Part II); the full-D1 run belongs to a later brief
t5b_competition.crossing_side: for crossing j and each name i live at tau_j with tau_i < tau_j <= tau_i + L: log ratio ln(n_after / n_before) of i's collapsed trades in [tau_j, tau_j + W) vs [tau_j - W, tau_j)
t5b_competition.control_side: same name i: moments t in i's own live span [tau_i, min(tau_i + L, 20:00 - W)] with t - W >= 04:00 and no D1 crossing other than i's own within [t - W, t + W]; drawn uniformly on a 1-second grid
t5b_competition.zero_counts: a window with zero trades on either side gives no log ratio; carried as a class with n
t5b_competition.outcome_used: none -- touches no outcome of j

negative_excursion.construction: per event and rung, 200 seeded shuffles of the demeaned bucket log returns (r_1..r_N), re-integrated from tau_price, run through the identical instrument (sigma_b re-estimated)
negative_excursion.pass: pooled u_peak matches the arcsine distribution AND mean rise_s within [0.70, 0.90], on every rung
negative_excursion.match_operationalised: KS distance between pooled u_peak and the arcsine CDF F(u) = (2/pi) arcsin(sqrt(u)) <= 0.05 on every rung. The brief gives no number; this threshold is declared here before the run. For scale: uniform vs arcsine is KS = 0.105.
negative_excursion.prediction_before_run: EXPECTED TO FAIL BY CONSTRUCTION. Demeaned returns sum to zero, so the re-integrated path ends where it starts: it is a discrete bridge, not a free walk. A cyclically exchangeable bridge has a UNIFORM argmax (not arcsine), and a Brownian bridge's expected maximum is sqrt(pi/8) = 0.627 of the path spread, not sqrt(2/pi) = 0.798. The declared criteria describe a free walk; the declared construction produces a bridge. Recorded here so a failure can be checked against its derivation rather than explained after the fact.
negative_excursion.diagnostic_arm: free walk: the same demeaned returns with independent random signs (Rademacher) and shuffled order -- zero drift in expectation, not a bridge. Evaluated against the same criteria. DIAGNOSTIC ONLY: it cannot change the declared verdict.

negative_acceleration.construction: per event, homogeneous Poisson tape: the event's own collapsed pre-tau trade count n placed uniformly on [04:00, tau]; the identical A2 ladder and stops
negative_acceleration.pass: per rung, pooled over events and draws: |median accel_k| < 0.1 AND spread consistent with sqrt(2/n)
negative_acceleration.spread_operationalised: SD of z_k = accel_k / sqrt(1/n_recent + 1/n_older) within [0.80, 1.25] per rung. Declared here before the run; the brief gives no number.
negative_acceleration.readable_rung: a rung is evaluated only where >= 100 valid (event, draw) values exist; thinner rungs are reported and labelled not readable

positive_excursion.construction: the same 200 shuffled paths per event and rung, plus an injected piecewise-linear drift in the event's OWN sigma_path units on that rung: +2.0 rising linearly from u = 0 to u = 0.3, then -1.5 falling linearly to u = 1; run through the identical instrument (sigma_b re-estimated on the injected path)
positive_excursion.pass: per rung: pooled median recovered u_peak within 0.3 +/- 0.05; pooled median recovered rise_s within 2.0 +/- 15% and fall_s within 1.5 +/- 15%

positive_acceleration.construction: per event, inhomogeneous Poisson tape with the event's own n and span H: rate r before a step at t_s, 2r after, normalised so the expected total is n. The step is placed exactly at the midpoint of rung m (t_s = tau - W_m/2), for m in {0, 1, 2, 3}
positive_acceleration.pass_literal: accel ~ ln 2 (+/- 0.2) on the rung whose halves straddle the step (k = m), ~ 0 (+/- 0.2) on rungs that do not
positive_acceleration.specification_gap_before_run: On rungs COARSER than the step (k < m) the step lies inside the recent half, and the exact expectation is ln(1 + 2^(k - m)): 0.405 at k = m-1, 0.223 at k = m-2, 0.118 at k = m-3. The literal '~ 0 on rungs that don't' cannot hold there for any correct instrument when m >= 1. Declared handling: the verdict is evaluated on rung k = m (ln 2 +/- 0.2) and rungs k > m (0 +/- 0.2) for every placement, and at m = 0 -- where no coarser rung exists and the literal criterion is complete -- on every rung. Rungs k < m are reported against ln(1 + 2^(k - m)) +/- 0.2, labelled, and flagged for Cooper; they do not enter the verdict. This is an interpretation of the pass text and is stated as one.
positive_acceleration.statistic: pooled median over events and draws, per (m, k)

null_parameter_sweep.construction: component medians across the bucket ladder {50, 100, 200}; count vs kernel A2 per rung
null_parameter_sweep.rung_dependent_rule: (max - min) of the three rung medians > 0.20 x |mean of the three| -> labelled rung-dependent; for components whose mean is within 0.05 of zero the absolute spread is reported instead of a ratio
null_parameter_sweep.pass: all medians reported and labelled; labelling is the output, not a failure

blindness.pass: sigma-unit and bp components identical to within 1e-9 (absolute) under rescaling, every event and rung
blindness.rounding: prices below $1.00 rounded to the $0.01 grid (half-up at the third decimal), prices >= $1.00 untouched; tau held at its exact-data instant; per-event change reported, no pass band

row_2.criterion: any T6 control fails its declared pass criterion (Amendment 2 criteria: amendment_2.controls)

row_3.criterion: any print after tau reaches an attention quantity (assertion fires)

row_4.criterion: tau_exact - tau_proxy_prime outside [-1, 61] s for more than 2% of D1, tau_proxy_prime recomputed with the same prior close as tau_exact (A1.1)

row_4_as_run_sensitivity.criterion: tau_exact - tau_proxy (v1's stored proxy, its own minute-bar close)

row_6.criterion: thin paths above 20% of the dev sample

row_7.criterion: T1 fallback (last_rth_print + unavailable) used for more than 10% of D1

charts.library: Plotly, standalone HTML, one chart per file, n on every bucket, no smoothing, outliers shown
charts.moved: run 1's charts moved from the top-level charts/attention_excursion/b1/ (A1.6)

outputs.run1_artifacts: results/attention_excursion/b1/artifacts/run1/ -- the stopped run's T1/T2 artifacts, kept as the record the amendment compares against
outputs.report_builder: research/attention_excursion_b1/build_report.py -- REPORT.md is generated from artifacts (A1.6, II.5)

cost_reference.use: reference lines only; no outcome is read in this brief

t1_prior_close_run1_superseded.calendar: exchange_calendars XNYS, pinned at the installed 4.13.2; prior session = cal.previous_session(event_date)
t1_prior_close_run1_superseded.prior_session_rows: prints whose sip_timestamp falls on the prior session's ET calendar date
t1_prior_close_run1_superseded.rule_1_auction: Amendment 6 override: a print carrying condition code 8 (Closing Prints) or 15 (Market Center Official Close) belongs to the session whose close it settles, regardless of timestamp. Prior close = the price of the LARGEST-SIZE {8,15} print on the prior session date; ties broken by code 8 first, then latest sip_timestamp.
t1_prior_close_run1_superseded.rule_1_why_largest_size: Surveyed before declaring (150 random D1 prior sessions): the code-8 closing cross prints once at the listing venue, and a code-15 official close at the same venue repeats its price and size; a second code-15 print from exchange 11 carries a different price in 116 of 139 sessions with a small size (e.g. CBRL 2020-03-23: 47,977 shares at the listing venue vs 120 at exchange 11). Largest size selects the listing venue's auction without hard-coding an exchange id.
t1_prior_close_run1_superseded.rule_2_fallback: no {8,15} print on the prior session date -> the last print by (sip_timestamp, sequence_number) with timestamp in [session_open, session_close] of the prior session (early closes from the calendar)
t1_prior_close_run1_superseded.unavailable: no print at all on the prior session date -> prior_close_available = FALSE, carried, never dropped. No reach back to T-2.
t1_prior_close_run1_superseded.condition_filter: none beyond the {8,15} rule -- same all-prints basis as the minute-bar build it replaces
t1_prior_close_run1_superseded.superseded_by: amendment_1 A1.2 -- the largest-size rule picked another venue's official close over the listing cross on 2,599 events

t1_prior_close.calendar: exchange_calendars XNYS, pinned at the installed 4.13.2; prior session = cal.previous_session(event_date)
t1_prior_close.prior_session_rows: prints whose sip_timestamp falls on the prior session's ET calendar date (Amendment 6: an auction print belongs to the session it settles, whatever its timestamp)

official_close.dictionary_attributes: updates_volume/high_low/last = false; 'dissemination of the official closing value, NOT an execution'

not_used.38: Corrected Consolidated Close (per listing market) -- named without full attributes; counted, not used
not_used.9: Cross Trade -- rides on the cross print ([8, 9, 41]); not a selector

listing_venue.source: results/phase_1b/artifacts/ticker_reference_snapshot.parquet, primary_exchange (the classification source of record; no API query). 3 D1 tickers carry two snapshot rows (LC, LYRA, SKLZ) that agree on venue; first row taken.
listing_venue.mapping_provenance: The repo holds no MIC -> Massive exchange-id table and the environment is offline (D14). Derived from a pre-run census (400 seeded D1 events per venue, all 11 XASE): XNAS-listed events carry their code-8 cross on exchange 12 in 361 of 400, XNYS-listed on exchange 10 in 358 of 400. XASE -> 1 is INFERRED, NOT VERIFIED: all 11 XASE-snapshot events crossed on exchange 10 (consistent with a later NYSE -> NYSE American transfer), and exchange 1 carries the code-8 cross on 3 XNYS-snapshot events.
listing_venue.code_15_note: Exchanges 11 and 12 disseminate a code-15 print for nearly every stock regardless of listing (census: code 15 on exchange 11 in 391/400 XNAS and 396/400 XNYS events). Code 15 is therefore only ever read on the listing venue.

precedence.rule: a code-8 print on the listing venue's exchange id on the prior session date; several -> the largest size, then the latest
no listing cross -> a code-15 print on the listing venue's exchange id; several -> the latest

the last print by (sip_timestamp, sequence_number) in [session_open, min(session_close, 16:00:00 ET)] of the prior session, excluding any print carrying code 8 or 15 from a venue other than the listing venue. The calendar close governs early-close days (13:00), per the CLAUDE.md session-calendar rule.
none of the above -> prior_close_available = FALSE, carried, never dropped; no reach back to T-2

t1_prior_close.listing_unknown: a D1 ticker with no snapshot venue skips rules 1-2 and is flagged listing_unknown (expected 0: all 15,763 resolve)
t1_prior_close.listing_venue_mismatch: TRUE when rule 1 fails on the snapshot venue while a code-8 cross print exists on the prior session on another listing-capable venue (exchange 1, 10 or 12) -- evidence the listing at the time differed from the snapshot. The resolution still follows the precedence; the flag carries the venue that crossed.
t1_prior_close.report: counts per source; revised - run1 close in bp; revised - minute-bar close in bp; where each of run 1's 2,599 other-venue picks now resolves

verification_II5: D1 row count = 15,763; dev = 50; sidecar = 6; slices partition D1 exactly
tau_ns dtype int64; tau_ns >= tau_proxy_prime minute start for every event with both (A1.1)
attention causality assertion wired into every attention function and exercised by a test that feeds a post-tau print and requires the raise
bucket volume conservation per event and rung
every count in REPORT.md read from an artifact by code at report-build time, not typed

summary: A1.1 row 4 and II.5 compare against tau_proxy_prime (same prior close); as-run kept as sensitivity
A1.2 T1 = listing_cross > listing_official > last_rth_print > unavailable, venue from the Phase 1b snapshot
A1.3 tau_close_sensitive (> 60 s) and tau_gap_close_s carried as facets
A1.4 spike guard stays 3%; tau_ns_guard15 carried
A1.5 if rows 1 and 4 clear, continue through T3-T7; T7 remains the HARD STOP
A1.6 CLAUDE.md D38 line, charts under results/, report generated by code
A1.7 Part III authorised on fix/e2-window-units

implementation_clarifications.committed: before T3-T6 ran, after the amended T1/T2 pass; none changes a declared rule or threshold
implementation_clarifications.t5b_crossing_set: j ranges over EVERY D1 crossing on the 50 dev-event dates (the brief restricts the dates, not the crossings); i over names live at tau_j with tau_i < tau_j
implementation_clarifications.t5_cross_section_windows: flow_share_k uses dollar volume over (tau_j - W_k, tau_j]; accel ranking uses j's own half-windows [tau_j - W_k, tau_j - W_k/2) and [tau_j - W_k/2, tau_j] on every live name's collapsed prints cut at tau_j
implementation_clarifications.t5_causality_test: attention.causality_test runs first in t5_attention.py and must pass before anything is built; its result is an artifact (t5_causality_test.json)
implementation_clarifications.t6_ks_with_atoms: u_peak takes values i/N; the KS distance to the arcsine CDF is evaluated on both sides of every atom (sup over the right-continuous ECDF and its left limit)
implementation_clarifications.t6_positive_acceleration_readable: same readability rule as the negative control: a (m, k) cell is evaluated only with >= 100 valid values; thinner cells are reported, labelled not readable
implementation_clarifications.t6_positive_acceleration_draws: Poisson counts on each side of the step (rate r before, 2r after, r = n / (H + W_m/2)), times uniform within each side
implementation_clarifications.t6_negative_acceleration_draws: fixed count n (the event's own collapsed pre-tau count), times uniform on [04:00, tau]
implementation_clarifications.t6_excursion_population: the 50 dev events x 3 rungs with a vector available and sigma_path > 0; sigma_zero synthetic paths are counted and excluded from the pooled statistic
implementation_clarifications.t6_blindness_scope: the excursion vector (sigma-unit and bp components), recomputed from rescaled prints and tau_price; tau held at its exact-data instant
implementation_clarifications.t3_profile_extent: profile computed 03:55-11:00 so the 10-20 minute reference level is defined through 10:30; charted 03:55-10:30

amendment_2.reruns: T4, T5, T5b, T6, then T7 HARD STOP (A2.10). T1-T3 are not re-run. Run 2 (bipower) T4-T6 artifacts and charts are kept under artifacts/run2/ and charts/run2/.

noise_scale.rule: sigma_path = sqrt(sum r_i^2) over the N log bucket returns (r_1 from tau_price) -- realised variance (A2.1)
noise_scale.descriptors: BV = (pi/2) (N/(N-1)) sum |r_i||r_(i-1)|; sigma_bv_path = sqrt(BV); jump_share = 1 - BV/RV. Carried, never a scale.
noise_scale.sigma_b_bp: now sigma_path / sqrt(N) (the per-bucket RV scale), in bp

peak_tie_rule.rule: peak = the earliest position whose price is within a relative 1e-9 of the maximum (log price >= max - ln(1 + 1e-9)) -- the first time the high is reached (A2.3)
carried: peak_tied (more than one position within tolerance)
peak_tie_span_u (volume-clock span from the first to the last tied position)

a2_per_rung_validity.rule: every rung k is computed and marked valid or invalid on its own (counting-noise stop and D22 floor per rung); no sequential stop (A2.4)
a2_per_rung_validity.fine_end: the ladder runs from k = 0 to the last rung whose half-window W_k/2 is at least the 10 ms collapse tolerance (below it two collapsed trades cannot share a half-window), capped at k_max = 40
a2_per_rung_validity.carried: valid-rung pattern per event (list of valid k), number of valid rungs; readings use valid rungs only
a2_per_rung_validity.kernel_check: computed on every valid rung where the scale field's edge rule defines it (history >= 4 x W_k)

t5b_defined_cells.rule: cells with W >= L are structurally undefined -- not run, reported as such (A2.5)

halt_rule.rule: halt_in_path = any inter-print gap in the path (tau to the first path print included) whose overlap with regular hours [session_open, session_close] of the event day is >= 300 s, OR an LULD-V3c label overlapping the path (A2.6). The calendar close governs early-close days.
halt_rule.descriptor: max_gap_outside_rth_s = the largest portion of any path gap lying outside regular hours -- a descriptor, not a halt
halt_rule.replaces: run 2's any-gap > 60 s proxy (48 of 49 dev paths flagged)

t3_boundary.status: RETIRED by Amendment 3 (A3.3): DA-4 replaced by segment anchoring; open_adjacent_0930 retired.

references.rule: simulated in the build at each rung's N with the same statistic and bucket construction, committed before the re-run (A2.2)

negative_bridge.construction: 200 seeded shuffles of the demeaned bucket returns per event and rung (unchanged)
negative_bridge.pass: two-sample KS distance between the pooled u_peak and the simulated Gaussian-bridge u_peak distribution at that N <= 0.05, AND |mean rise_s - simulated mean| <= 0.05, every rung

negative_free_walk.construction: 200 seeded draws with replacement from the demeaned bucket returns per event and rung (sum free)
negative_free_walk.pass: same criteria against the simulated Gaussian free walk at that N

positive.construction: the bridge path plus the injected drift in the event's own (RV) sigma_path units
positive.pass: pooled median recovered rise_s and fall_s each within +/-10% of the simulated median for the same injection at that N, AND pooled median u_peak within +/-0.05 of the simulated median u_peak, every rung
positive.reported: recovered versus injected (0.3 / 2.0 / 1.5) bias per rung, as an instrument property, never corrected

controls.negative_acceleration: unchanged criteria (|median| < 0.1, SD(z) in [0.80, 1.25], readable rungs >= 100 values), on the per-rung ladder
controls.positive_acceleration: unchanged criteria and placements, on the per-rung ladder
controls.null_parameter_sweep: unchanged rule, components under the RV scale
controls.blindness: unchanged criteria, re-run with the tie rule; ANEB 2022-06-22 must pass
controls.ks_two_sample: sup over atoms i/N of |F_control - F_reference|, both evaluated as right-continuous ECDFs on the same atom grid

amendment_2.step_zero_reference_line: T4's u_peak and rise_s charts draw the simulated discrete free-walk reference at each N, not the continuous 0.80 and arcsine (A2.2)
amendment_2.reading_bins: absolute, log-spaced bins in each measure's own units, n in every bin; no percentile sets any edge or threshold (A2.9). Brief 1 reads nothing; recorded for the reads that follow.

charts.plotly: inlined in every chart (A2.8, D14). Every chart in the tree is regenerated inline, including T1-T3's.

segment_anchor.rule: H = tau - the start of the clock segment tau falls in (A3.1)

segments.auction_open: session_open <= tau < session_open + 60 s -> no segment history (A3.2)
segments.regular: session_open + 60 s <= tau < session_close -> start session_open + 60 s (09:31:00)
segments.auction_close: session_close <= tau < session_close + 60 s -> no segment history (A3.2)
segments.after_hours: tau >= session_close + 60 s -> start session_close + 60 s (16:01:00)

segment_anchor.calendar: session_open / session_close from exchange_calendars XNYS for the event date (CLAUDE.md session-calendar rule): on early-close days the closing-cross minute is 13:00-13:01 and after hours start 13:01. The amendment's 16:00 / 16:01 are the full-day values of the same rule.
segment_anchor.segment_basis: clock time of tau (tau_anchor_segment). T2's tau_session_segment (Amendment 6 condition-code override) is carried alongside, unchanged.
segment_anchor.kernel_check: the one-sided kernel reads collapsed prints in [segment start, tau] only; its edge rule uses the segment-anchored H
segment_anchor.unchanged: A1 turnover still counts every share from 04:00 to tau; A3 unchanged; per-rung validity (A2.4) unchanged

amendment_3.II5_segment_assertion: for every rung, both half-windows [tau - W_k, tau - W_k/2) and [tau - W_k/2, tau] lie inside [segment start, tau] and intersect neither [session_open, session_open + 60 s) nor [session_close, session_close + 60 s); a violation raises (attention.assert_segment_windows)

auction_minute_class.rule: tau in [session_open, session_open + 60 s) or [session_close, session_close + 60 s) -> tau_in_auction_minute = TRUE, A2 unavailable (a label, never dropped); A1, A3, the cross-section's live set and the excursion are computed as normal. flow_share and accel_rank need j's rung windows, so they are unavailable for these events.
auction_minute_class.count_scope: reported for all of D1 (from t2_tau) and for the dev sample

t5b_matched_control.rule: for each (live name i, crossing j) pair and window W, control moments t are drawn from i's own live span with (a) the same octave of time since i's own crossing as tau_j: floor(log2(t - tau_i in seconds)) == floor(log2(tau_j - tau_i in seconds)); (b) the same clock segment as tau_j (premarket / regular / after hours; auction minutes are their own segments); (c) no other D1 crossing within +/- W; (d) t - W >= 04:00 and t + W <= 20:00. Drawn uniformly on a 1-second grid, controls_per_pair per pair, with the config seed (A3.5).
t5b_matched_control.no_match: a pair with no eligible moment is carried as status no_match, never filled from outside its bin
t5b_matched_control.defined_cells: unchanged from Amendment 2 A2.5 (W >= L undefined, not run)
t5b_matched_control.reported: matched controls per cell (pairs with >= 1 matched moment, pairs with no_match, matched moments drawn)

amendment_3.acceleration_controls: negative and positive acceleration controls generate their synthetic tapes over [segment start, tau] with the event's own collapsed count inside it; auction-minute events have no segment history and are excluded from these two controls (counted). Pass criteria unchanged.
report_additions: valid rungs per event, by segment, before (artifacts/run3/) and after the anchoring change
how many previously valid rungs straddled the open (window [tau - W_k, tau] intersecting [session_open, session_open + 60 s))
the from_nothing count, before and after
the auction-minute class count (D1 and dev)

rulings_a3_6.run1_run2_charts: left as the historical record; a README.md in each folder: 'generated by a superseded instrument; requires an internet connection to render.' run3/ gets the same README with the internet clause dropped (its charts are inlined).

brief2_diff._rule: Brief 2 section 1: the ONLY changes to Brief 1's frozen config (config/attention_excursion_b1.json at 99431b8, hash 658071fbe27f). Every Brief 1 key above is carried unchanged; each item here names what it supersedes. Checked by research/attention_excursion_b2/config_diff.py (escalation row 4).

R1.ruling: Brief 2 R1 (Cooper, 2026-09-25), with the cutoff Cooper chose on 2026-09-25 after the briefed rate rule was measured: 'Exact window count'
R1.rung_generation: rungs k = 0, 1, 2, ... are generated down to and including the first k whose whole window [tau - W_k, tau] holds fewer than 34 = 2 x n_min collapsed trades. The windows are nested, so the count never rises with k and no finer rung can reach n_min on both halves: the cutoff drops no rung that could be valid. Rungs 0 and 1 are always generated (a2_ignition reads them). The 10 ms half-window floor and k_max = 40 still apply. Window count = the ladder's own n_recent + n_older (collapsed prints in [tau - round(W_k), tau]).
R1.as_briefed_and_why_replaced: briefed: stop at the first k where the segment-average rate predicts fewer than 17 collapsed trades per half-window (n_seg / 2^(k+1) < 17). Measured on Brief 1's Amendment 3 dev rungs before this config was written: it would not generate 33 of the 249 valid rungs (18 of 49 events; 58 on 25 if the cutoff rung is excluded), because trading bunches up before tau. The exact count generates 344 of 881 rungs, keeps all 249 valid rungs and cuts from_nothing 225 -> 12.
R1.a2_ignition: TRUE when rung 0 or rung 1 is from_nothing (older half empty, recent half non-empty): silence in the older half of the segment, trading in the recent half. A label only, no prediction attached. NULL when A2 is unavailable.
R1.supersedes: the ladder extent of Amendment 2 A2.4 / Amendment 3 (every rung to the 10 ms floor); per-rung validity is unchanged

R2.ruling: Brief 2 R2 (Cooper, 2026-09-25): the competition control is re-matched on the population, not the same name
R2.log_ratio: unchanged from Brief 1: ln(n in [t, t + W) / n in [t - W, t)) of live name i's collapsed (10 ms) trades
R2.baseline_cell: (year, clock segment of t, liveness L, window W, age octave)
R2.age_octave: floor(log2(age in seconds)), age = t - tau_i for a baseline moment, tau_j - tau_i for a pair (the base-2 bins used elsewhere)
R2.baseline_moments: every live name i at every clock minute t (hh:mm:00 ET) with tau_i < t, i live at t for L (age <= L; rest of session: any age), and no D1 crossing other than i's own within [t - W, t + W]; pooled across names and dates in the year. i's own crossing is allowed because a pair at age < W carries it in the same place (Brief 1's control rule). No draws: every minute is used, so no seed.
R2.excess: observed pair log-ratio - the median log-ratio of the pair's baseline cell (finite log-ratios only)
R2.zero_counts: a window with zero trades on either side gives no log-ratio: a class with n on both sides, excluded from the median
R2.thin_cells: cells with fewer than 20 finite baseline moments are shown and labelled (baseline_thin) and not read
R2.defined_cells: W < L (Amendment 2 A2.5); windows_min [5, 15, 60]; liveness 15 min, 60 min, rest of session

R3.ruling: Brief 2 R3 (Cooper, 2026-09-25): the segment rule applies to the competition windows
R3.valid_window: a pair or baseline moment is valid only if [t - W, t + W] lies inside one clock segment -- premarket [04:00, open), regular [open + 60 s, close), after hours [close + 60 s, 20:00] -- and contains no cross minute ([open, open + 60 s), [close, close + 60 s)); open/close from the XNYS calendar (Amendment 3 A3.1)
R3.invalid: labelled window_crosses_segment and excluded on both sides; the share lost is reported per cell
R3.assertion: every retained window is re-checked in code and a violation raises (escalation row 3)

R4.ruling: Brief 2 R4 (Cooper, 2026-09-24): facet bins in absolute units; no percentile sets any bin edge

price_tier.on: tau_price (the price of the tau print, the decision instant's price)
price_tier.why_1: below $1 the minimum tick is $0.0001, above it $0.01 (Rule 612)

jump_share_band.why: log-spaced half-decade edges; jump_share = 1 - BV/RV can be zero or negative, so <= 0 is its own band
